newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firmer as speculation eases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firmer as speculation eases.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed an early slide to close firmer on Thursday after zigzagging through the session on speculation over testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, traders said.
"It was speculation more than anything. The peso slid to 7.95 per dollar, and then it recovered," a trader said.

"This means there was no real inflow or outflow of dollars, just plain speculation," he added. The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 1.3 and 0.2 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.9220/7.9270 and 7.9170/7.9220 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 2.2 centavos weaker at 7.9240/7.9270 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso weakened and then recovered in step with the U.S. long bond.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds weakened 7/32 to yield 7.02 percent in early trade after Greenspan hinted to a U.S. Congressional panel that U.S. interest rates might increase next week.
Nonetheless, the U.S. long bond was up 8/32 to yield 6.97 percent as the foreign exchange market closed in Mexico.
"A big local player that wanted to move the market triggerered speculation, but turnover was insufficient," a dealer said.
"That same player and a foreign counterpart together took profits (on dollars) and so the peso recovered," he added.
Dealers expected the peso to lose ground against the dollar due to corporate demand for dollars to meet month-end obligations.
Mexican financial markets will close on Friday, March 21, to honor 19th-century President and national hero Benito Jurez.
